chunks: Yunus narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding a man who said to his wife, 'I have not been given the virginity token.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no penalty upon him, because the virginity token can be lost through intercourse other than the primary act.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: His statement 'There is no penalty upon him' means there is no complete fixed punishment (hadd), although there is discretionary punishment (ta'zir) upon him according to what the first report contained.

key_terms.تَعْزِير: Discretionary punishment determined by the judge
key_terms.عَذْرَة: Virginity token (piece of tissue or cloth used to check for virginity)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling if a husband claims his wife was not a virgin but she was?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the claim of 'lack of virginity' (not being 'udhrat) does not automatically trigger the hadd of qadhf (fixed punishment for false accusation) because virginity can be lost through non-penile intercourse. Consequently, the husband faces ta'zir (discretionary punishment) rather than the strict hadd, a distinction emphasized by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan in al-istibsar. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance between definitive legal categories and contextual judicial discretion in marital disputes.
